_comment: Knowledge base config. Edit entity_types to change the allowed kb_extract_entities 'type' tag set.

entity_types.description: A real human person (full name and likely name variants).
An AKA / nickname / alternate spelling used by the same person (short label, not a full identity).
A company, nonprofit, agency, university, or group (brand/legal name).
A social username/screen name without a platform prefix (example: 'elonmusk', 'gouldieloxx'). Do not include the '@' unless you prefer consistency.
A full account identifier tied to a platform or profile URL (example: 'twitter:elonmusk', 'github:octocat', or https://profile.url).
A full HTTP/HTTPS URL to a specific resource/page (include scheme 'http://' or 'https://').
A GitHub/code repository identifier (example: 'owner/repo' or a repo URL).
An image file or image URL that can be analyzed for visual clues and metadata.
A phone number (include country code if possible).
A geographic location (city/region/country or approximate place).
A specific date or normalized date string (example: '2026-03-09' or '2024-05').
A document/artifact identifier (example: report title, PDF name, or 'case file' label).
A notable keyword/phrase that anchors investigation (example: campaign name, tag, tagline, or unique phrase).
Any entity that does not fit the categories above.

relation_types.description: Entity A and Entity B are both mentioned together in the same text excerpt (context relationship).
An alias/handle belongs to or refers to Entity B (e.g. alias -> person/account).
Entity A is affiliated with Entity B (work, education, membership, role, or involvement).
Entity A uses, operates, maintains, or is associated with Entity B as an account.
Entity A owns/controls/is responsible for Entity B as a domain/subdomain.
Entity A operates/maintains Entity B as a domain/subdomain.
Entity A hosts or is the owner/maintainer of Entity B as a repository.
Entity A (a URL/document) is explicitly linked to Entity B (e.g. a page contains evidence about the entity).
An image depicts/shows Entity B (person, object, place, event).
An image was extracted from a source URL/page/document.
An image or event is associated with a date/time.
An image or event is associated with a location.
Entity A is located in Entity B as a place/location.
Entity A (event) occurred on Entity B (date).
Entity A has (or is associated with) Entity B as an email address.
Entity A has (or is associated with) Entity B as a phone number.
Any other relationship that is clearly supported by text evidence.
